entries.name: GitHub Primer
observed_mechanisms: Separate color, spacing, and typography primitives from component implementations.
Use shared primitives to support product UI without coupling the reference registry to a project palette.
recommended_uses: Research token architecture, dense product UI, component anatomy, and state language.
Create a fresh Visual Evidence Card from current Primer sources when the target context is comparable.
prohibited_uses: Do not copy GitHub branding, exact tokens, icons, or composition into an unrelated product.
Do not treat this registry row as evidence.

entries.name: IBM Carbon Design System
observed_mechanisms: Systematic component reuse preserves visual and functional consistency across complex product surfaces.
Component documentation exposes problem-specific patterns rather than one generic card treatment.
recommended_uses: Research enterprise information density, data-heavy components, and state coverage.
Create a current evidence card before transferring any mechanism into a project basis.
prohibited_uses: Do not make Carbon's enterprise visual language a universal default.
Do not treat this registry row as evidence.

entries.name: Microsoft Fluent 2
observed_mechanisms: Separate global raw tokens from semantic alias tokens.
Tokenize color, typography, spacing, radius, stroke, shadow, duration, and easing so theming changes do not require hardcoded style recipes.
recommended_uses: Research semantic token layering, theming, accessibility modes, and cross-platform consistency.
Create a current evidence card when these mechanisms fit the target interaction model.
prohibited_uses: Do not import Fluent's visual identity merely because the target is a software product.
Do not treat this registry row as evidence.

entries.name: Adobe Spectrum
observed_mechanisms: Represent tokens as a required foundation dataset while components, mode sets, registries, and guidelines remain structured extensions.
Separate machine-readable design data from a single rendered theme.
recommended_uses: Research structured design data, component declarations, mode sets, and product-grade visual governance.
Create a fresh evidence card from current Spectrum sources when context matches.
prohibited_uses: Do not copy Adobe trade dress or assume creative-tool UI is suitable for every product.
Do not treat this registry row as evidence.

entries.name: daisyUI Themes
observed_mechanisms: A shared component vocabulary can support many distinct theme expressions.
Theme variables can be customized without changing component semantics.
recommended_uses: Expand the search space for theme variation and test whether component primitives are overly coupled to one look.
Use only as exploration unless stronger direct production evidence is separately recorded.
prohibited_uses: Do not select a built-in theme as project direction solely because it is available.
Do not ground a Visual Basis from this registry entry.

entries.name: tweakcn
observed_mechanisms: Visually edit theme parameters around reusable shadcn/Tailwind primitives.
Use theme variation to break the recognizable default appearance of a component stack.
recommended_uses: Explore parameter ranges and verify that a chosen component stack does not dictate project identity.
Use previews as hypotheses, not as proof of suitability.
prohibited_uses: Do not equate a preset with a validated project style.
Do not ground a Visual Basis from this registry entry.

entries.name: UI UX Pro Max
observed_mechanisms: Expose a broad searchable vocabulary of styles, palettes, typography pairings, product categories, and UX checks.
Provide candidate search terms that can widen exploration before evidence is collected.
recommended_uses: Generate diverse search hypotheses and names for visual mechanisms the team may otherwise overlook.
Use its categories only to seed external research against direct sources.
prohibited_uses: Never accept product-to-style, product-to-palette, or font-pair recommendations as evidence-backed defaults.
Never copy its generated design-system output into production without independent project evidence.
